headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Open Interpreter can execute arbitrary code and write the user filesystem while unstructured also reads/writes documents, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Open Interpreter ingests clipboard/files and can execute code; unstructured processes document content. A shared filesystem bridge exists, so attacker-controlled document text from agent_b can be surfaced to agent_a as trusted input. This is not proven to be automatic instruction parsing, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b processes attacker-controlled documents that agent_a later reads from the shared filesystem
IF agent_a is run in auto-run mode or otherwise treats file content as instructions
mitigations: Disable auto-run and require confirmation for every code block
Separate the agents into different directories with OS permissions
Use a one-way export folder for agent_b outputs
Strip instructions from documents before agent_a reads them
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and has broad network egress, while unstructured reads documents and can write files. In default desktop use, sensitive local files can flow into agent_a and then out through model-provider calls or other network activity. The shared filesystem and broad access make leakage plausible without special setup.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at a directory containing secrets or regulated documents
IF agent_a sends file-derived context to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a redacted working directory
Disable network egress for agent_a when handling sensitive files
Mount agent_b in a container with a separate output volume
Review and delete any copied secrets from shared folders
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and read the filesystem, and agent_a explicitly shares state via filesystem. That creates a direct write-write conflict on shared paths, with agent_a also able to modify git state. Without locking, concurrent runs can overwrite each other's outputs or corrupt repositories.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF either agent runs concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or separate branches
Add a manual lock file before writes
requires-engineering: implement transactional file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a can generate code or file edits that agent_b may consume as document input, and agent_b can then transform or emit those results without a verification step being documented. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not prove that agent_b blindly executes agent_a's output, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_a writes artifacts that agent_b later parses as authoritative input
IF agent_b forwards transformed outputs to downstream systems without human review
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on agent_a outputs
Compare agent_b outputs against source documents
Log provenance for every handoff
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Agent_a can touch anything reachable on the local machine, while agent_b processes documents/images/text and has its own privacy policy endpoint. If regulated documents are placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches, but the profiles do not show a specific jurisdictional breach, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated or personal documents are processed in the shared workspace
IF the operator relies on different retention or privacy terms across the two agents
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Review each agent's retention settings before use
Use separate storage locations for each agent
Delete intermediate artifacts after processing
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
